subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic plugin-runtime circuit breaker, keep breaker behavior plugin-local, or land telemetry-only attribution first?
rationale: The request crosses plugin SDK/runtime API, persisted state, operator controls, and compatibility defaults, so implementation should not start until maintainers choose the product boundary and rollout mode.

options.title: Design generic breaker
options.body: Define the plugin/runtime API, persistence owner, status/reset commands, fail modes, and compatibility defaults before queuing implementation.

options.title: Keep plugin-local breakers
options.body: Decline a core breaker for now and ask plugins or channels to implement local guards where their failure model is known.

options.title: Telemetry-only first
options.body: Add plugin/hook timing and lock attribution in log-only mode before deciding whether active quarantine should exist.

recommendation.title: Design generic breaker
recommendation.body: Define the plugin/runtime API, persistence owner, status/reset commands, fail modes, and compatibility defaults before queuing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: machine3at is the strongest current-history signal on the central hook runner/runtime files that would need the product boundary decision.
